aiExplanation: This function finds the **lexicographically smallest** list of indices in `word1` that spell out `word2` as a subsequence, while allowing **at most one character mismatch**. It works in two passes: the first loop scans `word1` **backwards** and fills the `last` array, where `last[j]` records the latest position in `word1` at which `word2[j]` can still be matched exactly — this tells the second pass how long it can afford to wait before committing to a character. The second loop then scans **forwards** greedily: at each position `i` it checks whether the current character matches `word2[j]` (`sameChar`); if it doesn't match, the position is skipped when the single allowed mismatch (`skipped`) has already been used, or when it's still safe to wait because the remaining characters can be matched later (`i >= last[j + 1]` guards against waiting too long). Otherwise the index is pushed into `res` — burning the mismatch flag if the characters differ — and `j` advances to the next character of `word2`. Finally, if all `m` characters were matched (`j === m`) the index list is returned; otherwise an empty array signals that no valid sequence exists.
